title: Debug breadcrumbs & microtasks — Nora Park
content:
Purpose: Quick daily scratchpad for immediate triage steps, tiny experiments, and microtasks to reduce p99 tail for small chat sessions. Not a final doc, just breadcrumbs for handoff.

Symptom observed (03/10 evening): p99 spike from 180ms -> 620ms on small single-token requests on dedicated pool A (g4dn-like). Spike started ~18:32 UTC, lasted ~45m. No CPU/GPU saturation in metrics. Spike correlated with increased short-lifetime sessions (session churn).

Immediate hypotheses:
- KV cache thrash from many tiny sessions (cache churn + lock contention).
- Prefix-caching path falling back to cold start for many different session IDs.
- Background compaction job (mem reclaim) coinciding causing short GC pauses in python shim.
- Networking flaps causing retries + queueing at ingress.

Quick checks done:
- grep logs for session-open around spike -> many opens with unique session ids (session-ids-12k).
- looked at runtime /metrics endpoint: kernel_queue_time p50 ~2ms, p99 ~58ms during spike window.
- perf top on node (sample): no obvious NVidia contended kernels, userland shows python worker wait.

Immediate microtasks (today):
- [ ] Add temporary debug flag to log KV-cache hit/miss per session id in staging (INF-2710). Low cost: +1 field to request tracing. (assigned Liam)
- [ ] Roll out short-lived test that pins small batch size and disables prefix-cache for a canary subset (10% traffic) -> measure p99. (me)
- [ ] Add histogram for per-request lock-wait (mutex_wait_us) to runtime metrics. Goal: surface contention. (Aria)
- [ ] Check recently merged PR that touched session id hashing (PR 482) for accidental high-entropy session key change. (me)

Notes / commands to run:
- tail -n 500 /var/log/runtime/runtime.log | grep "open_session" | sed -n '1,200p'
- curl -s http://staging-metrics:9090/metrics | grep kernel_queue_time_histogram
- quick local repro: script/mini_session_repro.py --rate 120 --unique-session-per-request true --seq-len 1

Observations to capture in ticket INF-2799: attach sample trace, timeline, node metrics, and short repro script. Need to quantify delta when prefix-cache disabled.

Unresolved / questions:
- Is there an autoscaler scale-up event that changes pod placement mid-spike? Check cluster events in 18:00-19:00 UTC.
- Could ephemeral connections to KMS for tokenization be adding latency when sessions are new? (unlikely but note)

Meeting notes (03/11 daily):
- Agreed: first step is lightweight observability (lock-wait histograms + per-session cache hit ratio). Do that today.
- Canary disables prefix-cache for 10% traffic to see effect; rollback fast if throughput drops.

Next day plan (03/12):
- Run canary, collect 6-hour window metrics, validate whether p99 reduces to <250ms.
- If reduced, prepare rollout plan with gradual ramp and QC checks (latency, cost increase).

Misc small ideas (future):
- Consider session-id sharding so KV cache slices by hash prefix to reduce lock surface.
- Explore per-session small TTL for prefix-cache so churn doesn't push global evictions.

Handoff: copy this note to INF-2710 and tag @oncall in #infra-runtime with a 1-line summary.

Random TODO brain dump:
- scrub old traces in S3 (cost).
- follow up with SRE on network telemetry retention.
- schedule 1:1 with Aria to review lock instrumentation results.
